cards.explanation: The answer is True. Abraham had six sons by Keturah and still, "Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac." Everything, friends. That's the whole bakery going to one stamper. And he didn't leave the other sons empty-handed either, as we'll see in a moment (Genesis 25:5-6).

The answer is gifts to take with them. "…Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines…" while he was still alive, and then he sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east (Genesis 25:6). Gifts first, then the goodbye. The text doesn't say what the gifts were, so I won't guess.

The answer is old and contented. Genesis 25:8 says Abraham "…breathed his last and died, old and contented…" Contented, friends. After 175 years, that's a man who is at peace. I'd bake a whole batch for that kind of ending.

The answer is his wife Sarah. "Abraham was buried there with his wife Sarah." (Genesis 25:10). The cave of Machpelah was in the field he bought from the Hittites, so the two of them rest in the same place. I think there's something tender about that.

The answer is blessed. "After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac…" (Genesis 25:11). Abraham had been blessed by the LORD too (Genesis 24:1), and now Isaac gets his own. I think that's a good way to see the story isn't ending when the funeral does. God's blessing was already sitting there waiting for Isaac, like a fresh batch cooling on the rack.

The answer is Hagar. Hagar the Egyptian was Sarah's maidservant, and she bore Ishmael to Abraham (Genesis 25:12). The text names her by her place in the household, so I'll do the same, friends. Ishmael has his own account right here.

The answer is False. Genesis 25:18 says Ishmael's descendants "…lived in hostility toward all their brothers." Not peace, friends, hostility. I think that's a heavy note to end on. The text doesn't say more about why.
